findings.title: Backup code can bypass the password when combined with a dummy TOTP field
findings.body: Password verification at the top of authorize() only runs when credentials.totpCode is absent, while this new branch runs whenever credentials.backupCode is present and never validates the supplied TOTP value. An attacker can call the public credentials endpoint directly with an email, any totpCode value, and a valid backup code, skipping password verification entirely. A backup code therefore becomes a single-factor credential instead of a replacement for only the authenticator factor.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be reused concurrently
findings.body: The code performs a read, indexOf check, and separate prisma.user.update() to null out the used code. Two parallel login requests with the same backup code can both read the original encrypted list, both find the code, and both authenticate before either update is visible. This violates the stated exactly-once property of backup codes; consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update or locking.

findings.title: Successful 2FA enablement is only reported to the parent from the backup-codes Close button
findings.body: handleEnable() now replaces onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), and the only remaining call to onEnable() is the footer Close button for that step. If the dialog is dismissed through its normal onOpenChange path (close control, Escape, or outside interaction) after the server has already enabled 2FA, the parent is never notified and keeps rendering 2FA as disabled until a reload, while the modal also remains on the stale backup-codes step when reopened.

findings.title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: The migration leaves backupCodes null for every existing 2FA user, and this setup endpoint is the only place in the PR that generates backup codes, but it rejects anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. Those users are nevertheless offered the Lost access backup-code flow at login and when disabling 2FA, and will only receive MissingBackupCodes, despite the error copy telling them to generate codes in settings where no such action exists.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison rejects uppercase and whitespace-padded entry
findings.body: Generated codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')), but verification only strips '-' and does an exact indexOf match, with no trim() or case normalization; the disable endpoint repeats the same logic. A user who manually transcribes a saved code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, is told the code is incorrect even though they supplied the right code. The supplied value should be normalized (trim, remove dashes, lowercase) before comparison in both verification paths.

findings.title: resetState leaves backup codes, TOTP secret, and the download URL in memory
findings.body: resetState() clears only the password, error message, and step. It does not clear backupCodes, secret, dataUri, or backupCodesUrl, and never revokes the Blob object URL containing all plaintext backup codes. The modal component stays mounted on the settings page, so the full set of recovery codes and the TOTP secret remain retrievable in component state and via the still-valid blob URL long after the backup-codes screen is closed.

findings.title: No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only checks that the backup-codes download has the right filename, that copy shows a toast, and that the dialog closes, with explicit TODOs for checking file contents and for login/disable backup-code tests. The security-critical new behavior - login with a correct backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use invalidation of a consumed code, users with no stored codes, and disabling 2FA with a backup code - has no automated coverage, so regressions in these paths would ship undetected.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField component makes that control unreachable by keyboard for all password fields across the app, not just in the 2FA modals touched by this PR. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer toggle password visibility, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes.
